title: Girls without tongues
author: Ipsita Sarangi/ଈପ୍ସିତା ଷଡ଼ଙ୍ଗୀ
text:
Some girls are born in to the woman
Before they even fully grasp
They are compelled to shoulder every duty of womanhood.

Being a mother to younger siblings
managing a multitude of responsibilities
Their lives trudge on tethered to the soil
Having heard words like "belonging to others"
and "destined to another`s home" since birth,
They can never truely bring themselves to believe
that the very home they inhabit is their own.

To whom does a woman truely belong
Whose life does she carry as her own
With whose identity does she move to another`s home
Unable to ever break free from these ties,
These daughters meet their end within that very cocoon.

These girls
with every breath, they seek the well-being of households:
Even in sleep, the burdens of two families weigh upon them,
In dreams, they gather the responsibilities of the entire world
Grappling with it all throughout their lives.

Like sweat evaporating over a burning hearth
They are curified again and again
yet, if the need arises, they return
Dripping their veils over backs bloodied by thorns
They set themselves once more to their daily toil.

These girls were born without a tongue
But some words remain, like coals
Deep within their burning,crimson hearts;
The impersonal lines are like poetry.

These lines burns to the girls
Though some may perish in the process
deep within those hearts,
Those embers find no solace,
no soothing touch of a sweet, flowing stream.

They have come to believe
that a vast ocean of a happiness
is forbidden to them
yet, even today they wait
awaiting the Bhagirathi of an unheared divine melody.

Let`s transform their silence
their endurance
and their sighs
in to a vessel for seeking happiness
let`s!
∎
Translated from original Odia by Bandana Sahoo
